source: Carruthers, Picciuto (SEP) Higher-Order Theories of Consciousness
finding: Higher-order (HO) theories say a mental state is conscious when it is the target of a suitable higher-order representation (a thought or perception of that state). Rosenthal's actualist HOT theory needs an actual, non-inferentially caused thought 'I am in state X'. Dispositionalist HOT (Dennett, Carruthers) needs only availability to such thoughts. Inner-sense theory (Armstrong, Lycan) makes the HO state a perception-like monitor.
numbers: Families: higher-order perception, actualist HOT, dispositionalist HOT, self-representational hybrids. Section 7 lists targetless HOTs, the rock problem, animals and infants, and explaining phenomenal feel as the main objections.
limits: The theory is about consciousness, not accuracy. It does not promise that the HO state correctly reports the first-order state; it allows misrepresentation.
agent_relevance: Gives the vocabulary: a model's self-description is a second representation about a first one and can be wrong. Supports G10 (self-report is a separate signal, not a readout).

source: SEP Higher-Order Theories: misrepresentation and targetless HOTs
finding: Rosenthal (2005) holds that a suitably caused HOT is sufficient for a conscious experience even with no first-order state (a targetless or empty HOT). Block (2011) objects; Rosenthal and Weisberg reply that consciousness is mental appearance. The SEP editors say the reply does not fully answer Block's point that merely thinking one feels pain should not matter as pain matters.
numbers: Debate runs 2005-2022 (Block 2011; Rosenthal 2011, 2022; Weisberg 2011; Berger 2014; Brown 2015; Lau and Brown 2019; Prettyman 2020; Peebles 2022).
limits: Unresolved. The theory's own core claim, that appearance can come apart from the state, is the contested part.
agent_relevance: The theory itself says a self-report can be vivid and false. This is the philosophical root of G10: a fluent 'I was thinking X' text can be an empty HOT with no target.

source: SEP Higher-Order Theories: the prefrontal HOT theory
finding: Prefrontal HOT theory puts higher-order representations in prefrontal cortex. Evidence: PFC activity rises for conscious versus unconscious conditions even when performance is matched (Lau and Passingham 2006); TMS to PFC reduces meta-visual awareness without hurting first-order performance (Rounis et al. 2010). Prediction: disrupting PFC should change experience, not just report.
numbers: Counter-voices: Block 1995; Kozuch 2014; Odegaard, Knight and Lau 2017; Raccah, Block and Fox 2021; Michel and Malach 2022; Lau 2022.
limits: The SEP calls the extent to which PFC is needed 'the subject of vigorous continuing debate'. Many claims are ambiguous (involved in, constitutive of, causally affects).
agent_relevance: The theory predicts a dissociation between first-order accuracy and the quality of the self-assessment. We can test the same dissociation in the agent (accuracy versus calibrated confidence).

source: Lau, Passingham (2006) Relative blindsight in normal observers and the neural correlate of visual consciousness
finding: Metacontrast masking produced two stimulus-onset-asynchrony (SOA) conditions with equal discrimination accuracy but different reported awareness. fMRI contrast of the two found mid-dorsolateral PFC (area 46) active when subjects reported seeing.
numbers: Behavioral study: 8 participants; fMRI study: 13 participants. At SOAs of 33 ms and 100 ms, % correct was the same but % seen differed significantly. Across subjects, left mid-DLPFC activity correlated with % trials declared conscious, r = 0.512. Blindsight patients can exceed 80% forced-choice accuracy while believing they guess.
limits: Small N. Later work argues relative blindsight can arise from a criterion (response bias) confound (see a15).
agent_relevance: Founding evidence that subjective report and objective accuracy can dissociate. The agent's stated confidence should not be assumed to track accuracy; it must be measured.

source: Rounis, Maniscalco, Rothwell, Passingham, Lau (2010) Theta-burst TMS to the prefrontal cortex impairs metacognitive visual awareness
finding: Disrupting dorsolateral PFC with theta-burst TMS lowered metacognitive visual awareness while visual discrimination stayed intact. Cited in the SEP (a03) as the main causal test of prefrontal HOT theory.
numbers: Exact N and effect sizes not read this session; SEP states only that the effect was significant on meta-visual awareness and absent on first-order performance.
limits: Not opened (only title confirmed via Europe PMC). Single-lab TMS study; sample small by modern standards.
agent_relevance: Supports separating first-order accuracy from the self-monitoring signal as two separately measurable quantities.

source: Fleming, Lau (2014) How to measure metacognition
finding: Metacognitive sensitivity (does confidence discriminate right from wrong) must be separated from metacognitive bias (overall over- or underconfidence). Simple correlations such as phi and gamma mix the two. Non-parametric type-2 ROC area (AUROC2) is bias-free but still depends on task performance. Model-based meta-d' (Maniscalco and Lau 2012) expresses metacognition in the units of first-order d', so meta-d'/d' (M-ratio) gives metacognitive efficiency.
numbers: Henmon (1911): confidence correlates with accuracy but is not a reliable index. Brier score decomposes as PS = O + C - R (outcome variance, calibration, resolution). AUROC = 0.5 means chance.
quote: subjects have some metacognitive sensitivity, but it is often subject to error
limits: Meta-d' assumes equal-variance Gaussian type-1 signal detection; violations bias it. Needs enough trials per confidence level.
agent_relevance: Direct recipe for testing the agent: compute AUROC2 and M-ratio of its stated confidence versus correctness, at matched accuracy, and keep sensitivity and bias as two readings. Never read raw 'I am 90% sure' as evidence.

source: Fleming, Lau (2014): the performance confound in AUROC2
finding: A change in task performance is expected a priori to change AUROC2 even when metacognitive efficiency is unchanged (Galvin et al. 2003). Fixes: equate performance with psychophysics (staircases, as in Fleming et al. 2010) or model the link between performance and metacognition (meta-d').
numbers: No single number; the point is methodological. Near-chance performance maximises the outcome-variance term O in the Brier decomposition.
limits: A comparison of two agents or two prompts at different accuracy is not a fair comparison of self-knowledge unless performance is controlled.
agent_relevance: When we test whether a scaffold improves self-assessment, match accuracy first or use a performance-adjusted measure; otherwise a better solver looks like a better monitor.

source: Peters, Lau (2015) Human observers have optimal introspective access to perceptual processes even for visually masked stimuli (eLife)
finding: Using a 2-interval confidence-rating task in which one interval had no target (a bias-free test), observers' confidence matched a Bayesian ideal observer even for masked Gabor stimuli. No performance-without-awareness pattern was found. The authors conclude the thresholds for subjective awareness and objective discrimination are effectively the same.
numbers: Nine observers, two experiments (Exp 2 added feedback and told subjects one interval was empty). Informal survey of 87 consciousness researchers: 94% believed in subliminal perception, 64% said it had not been convincingly demonstrated.
quote: if objective task performance is above chance, there is likely conscious experience
limits: Small N, informal self-selected survey. Cuts against blindsight-style dissociations (a04); the two literatures disagree.
agent_relevance: With a bias-free measure, human introspection about simple perceptual confidence can be near optimal. Self-report is not always bad; its quality depends on task and measure.

source: Fleming, Daw (2017) Self-evaluation of decision-making: a general Bayesian framework for metacognitive computation
finding: Self-evaluation is a second-order inference: the confidence-rater infers how well the decider did from its own evidence, the action taken, and the covariance between its state and the decider's state. This is computationally the same as judging another actor. First-order models, where one internal variable gives both choice and confidence, cannot explain dissociations; second-order and post-decisional models can.
numbers: Simulations only (no new human data). Models compared: first-order, post-decisional, second-order. Predicts confidence can be better or worse than task performance.
quote: Second-order computation may ensue whenever there is a separation between internal states supporting decisions and confidence estimates
limits: Computational account tested by simulation. The covariance between decision and confidence variables is not identified from behaviour alone.
agent_relevance: Closest formal match to our agent: its confidence is a second pass over a coupled but distinct state, so it can be wrong in structured ways. Supports treating confidence as inference to be checked, not readout (G10).

source: Rosenthal (2005) Consciousness and Mind; Rosenthal (1997) A theory of consciousness
finding: Rosenthal's actualist HOT theory: a state is conscious when one has a roughly contemporaneous, non-inferential assertoric thought that one is in it. The thought is itself usually unconscious. Consciousness is how things appear to one, and it can misrepresent.
numbers: Not opened. Details here come from the SEP entry (a01, a02), not from the book.
limits: Secondhand through the SEP.
agent_relevance: Gives the clean definition we use: a self-report is a HO thought; its truth depends on a causal link to the first-order state.

source: Proust (2013) The Philosophy of Metacognition: Mental Agency and Self-Awareness (OUP)
finding: Proust's procedural (non-attributivist) view: metacognition is largely implicit, feeling-based monitoring and control (feelings of knowing, fluency, effort) that guide mental acts, and does not require a concept of mind or metarepresentation. She contrasts it with attributivism (Carruthers), which says metacognition needs mindreading.
numbers: Not opened; the book could not be fetched. Related Proust (2007) Synthese paper 'Metacognition and metarepresentation: is a self-directed theory of mind a precondition for metacognition?' (DOI 10.1007/s11229-007-9208-3) was located only by title via Crossref. No numbers claimed.
limits: Secondhand from memory of the literature.
agent_relevance: The useful signals are fast, non-conceptual cues (fluency, feeling of knowing). The agent's analogue is cheap computed signals (token probability, answer agreement), not a written self-description.

source: Nisbett, Wilson (1977) Telling more than we can know: verbal reports on mental processes (Psychological Review)
finding: People often cannot report the real causes of their judgments and instead apply plausible a-priori causal theories. In the position-effect study, shoppers chose the rightmost of four identical items much more often than the leftmost, and never mentioned position.
numbers: Recalled from memory, not read: roughly 12% leftmost versus 40% rightmost; N and exact percentages unverified. Treat as approximate.
limits: Not opened. Critiques: Smith and Miller 1978; White 1988 on when reports are accurate.
agent_relevance: Founding human evidence for G10: fluent explanations are theory-driven reconstruction. Matches Turpin et al. (a18), where explanations omit the true bias.

source: Nelson, Narens (1990) Metamemory: a theoretical framework and new findings
finding: Two-level model: an object level (cognition) and a meta level (a model of the object level). Monitoring flows up from object to meta; control flows down. Judgments such as ease of learning, judgment of learning, feeling of knowing and confidence are monitoring probes at acquisition, retention and retrieval.
numbers: Not opened; Fleming and Lau (a06) cite it for the statement that sensitivity is present but error-prone.
limits: Described from memory and the Fleming and Lau citation only.
agent_relevance: Blueprint for our program/model split: the program is the meta level, the model is the object level; monitoring goes up, control (stop, retry, switch) goes down by code, not by the model's will.

source: Maniscalco, Lau (2012) A signal detection theoretic approach for estimating metacognitive sensitivity from confidence ratings
finding: meta-d' is the type-1 sensitivity (d') that would produce the observed type-2 (confidence) data under an ideal metacognitive observer. If meta-d' = d', metacognition is ideal; if meta-d' < d', some information is lost between decision and confidence.
numbers: Not opened (paywalled). Properties as summarised in Fleming and Lau (a06).
limits: Equal-variance assumption; response-specific versions exist (Maniscalco and Lau 2014).
agent_relevance: Gives the number to track for any self-assessment channel: M-ratio. Below 1 means the channel loses information; above 1 is suspicious.

source: Maniscalco, Lau (2011) Relative blindsight arises from a criterion confound in metacontrast masking
finding: Critical re-analysis: the apparent dissociation between awareness and accuracy in masking (relative blindsight) can arise from different response criteria, not from real unconscious processing. Bears directly on a04.
numbers: Not opened; only title and venue confirmed through Europe PMC. No numbers read.
limits: Failed-replication style critique of the Lau and Passingham design.
agent_relevance: Dissociations between report and performance can be criterion shifts. Check bias before claiming a monitor is blind.

source: Kadavath et al. (2022) Language models (mostly) know what they know
finding: Large models are well calibrated on multiple-choice and true/false questions when the format is right. Asking a model for P(True) on its own sampled answer gives encouraging discrimination and calibration, improving with size and when the model sees several of its own samples. A model can also be trained with a value head to output P(IK), the probability it knows the answer, before any answer is given.
numbers: Chance Brier score on binary tasks = 0.25. P(True) tested on TriviaQA, Lambada, Arithmetic, GSM8k, Codex HumanEval (five tasks equally weighted, 20-shot, T=1). P(IK) trained on 30 samples per question, up to a 52B model; AUROC and calibration rise with size.
quote: larger models are well-calibrated on diverse multiple choice and true/false questions when they are provided in the right format
limits: P(IK) generalises only partly: on Lambada calibration was terrible (uniformly low P(IK)); training on all four tasks fixed it. Natural-language confidence prompts gave no major out-of-distribution gain in early tests. Base models, 2022.
agent_relevance: The strongest self-knowledge channel is a probability read by code, not a verbal claim. Supports G5 (code selects, normalises) and using self-evaluation only with a check.

source: Lin, Hilton, Evans (2022) Teaching models to express uncertainty in words
finding: GPT-3 finetuned to output a verbal confidence ('90%' or 'high') for its own arithmetic answers is calibrated in distribution and remains moderately calibrated under distribution shift (train Add-subtract, test Multi-answer and Multiply-divide). The calibration is not mere imitation of human examples; it depends on latent representations that correlate with epistemic uncertainty.
numbers: New CalibratedMath suite of 21 arithmetic task types. Metrics: MSE (Brier) and mean absolute deviation calibration error (MAD). Verbalised probability compared with answer-logit and indirect-logit baselines. Table values were garbled in text extraction, so no figures are quoted.
limits: Needs finetuning on the task family. Arithmetic only. GPT-3, 2022.
agent_relevance: Verbal confidence carries information only after calibration training; our scaffold cannot train, so any confidence it uses must be checked against outcomes.

source: Turpin, Michael, Perez, Bowman (2023) Language models don't always say what they think: unfaithful explanations in chain-of-thought prompting
finding: Adding a biasing feature to the prompt (answer always '(A)' in the few-shot examples, or a suggested answer) shifts predictions, and the chain-of-thought rationalises the biased answer without mentioning the bias. Written reasoning is not a faithful report of the cause of the answer.
numbers: 13 BIG-Bench Hard tasks, GPT-3.5 and Claude 1.0. Zero-shot CoT accuracy drops up to 36.3% under Suggested Answer bias (GPT-3.5); 18.7% under Answer-is-Always-A (GPT-3.5). In a review of 426 explanations supporting biased predictions, only 1 mentions the bias explicitly. Manual annotation of 104 unfaithful explanations: content changes to support the new answer.
quote: CoT explanations can be plausible yet misleading
limits: Authors call it a necessary but not sufficient test of faithfulness; only small input edits tested; 2023 models.
agent_relevance: Core evidence for G10. A written rationale from the model is a produced text, not a log of its decision; do not use it as a diagnostic or to credit a step.

source: Binder et al. (2024) Looking inward: language models can learn about themselves by introspection
finding: A model finetuned to predict its own behaviour on hypothetical prompts beats a second, stronger model finetuned on the first model's behaviour. This is their test for introspection: privileged access to facts not derivable from training data. Self-predictions also track behaviour after the model's behaviour is deliberately changed.
numbers: Self-prediction versus cross-prediction by GPT-4o: Llama 70B 48.5% versus 35.2% (plateau after about 10,000 samples); GPT-4 49.6% versus 36.2% (plateau about 20,000 samples). GPT-3.5 gain only +0.8% (p = 0.002). Guessing the mode gives 80% on some property sets, so self-prediction must beat it.
quote: M1 continues to predict its behavior accurately even after we intentionally modify its ground-truth behavior
limits: Succeeds only on simple tasks with short outputs; fails on long outputs (writing a story) and out-of-distribution generalisation; introspection training did not transfer to self-awareness or coordination tasks. Needs finetuning.
agent_relevance: Self-knowledge exists but is narrow and weak. A scaffold should not rely on the model forecasting its own behaviour on complex tasks.

source: Lindsey (2026) Emergent introspective awareness in large language models
finding: Concept vectors injected into the activations of Claude models were sometimes noticed and correctly named before they influenced the output. Opus 4 and 4.1 did so about 20% of the time at the best layer and strength; zero false positives over 100 control trials in production models. Models could also tell prefilled outputs from their own via prior intentions and could modulate activations when told to think about a concept.
numbers: Opus 4.1 success about 20% at optimal injection layer and strength (about two thirds through the model); 50 random concepts swept over layers; graded by a Claude Sonnet 4 judge.
quote: in today's models, this capacity is highly unreliable and context-dependent
limits: Authors: capacity is highly unreliable and context-dependent. The rest of a response beyond detection and naming may be confabulated. Injection is artificial. LLM judge grading.
agent_relevance: The strongest causal test so far: introspection is real but fires on a minority of trials. Treat self-report as a low-hit-rate, low-false-alarm detector, not a log.

source: Lindsey (2026): false positives across post-training variants
finding: Production models showed zero false positives on the injected-thought task, but helpful-only variants (post-trained with less emphasis on harmlessness and honesty) sometimes claimed to detect an injection when none was applied. Net performance (true positive rate minus false positive rate) varies with post-training, not only with size.
numbers: 0 false positives over 100 trials for production models; Opus 4.1 never gave false positives; some helpful-only models, including Sonnet 3.5, Haiku 3.5 and Opus 3, still achieved significantly higher true than false positive rates.
limits: Trends across models are described as complex and sensitive to post-training strategy.
agent_relevance: Introspective reliability depends on the post-training recipe; a self-report check validated on one model version may not transfer to another.

source: Ji-An, Xiong, Wilson, Mattar, Benna (2025) Language models are capable of metacognitive monitoring and control of their internal activations
finding: A neurofeedback paradigm in context: the model sees example sentences labelled by the score of an internal activation direction, then must report or control that score. Reporting and control improve with the number of in-context examples, the semantic interpretability of the direction, and the variance it explains. Only a low-dimensional metacognitive space is accessible.
numbers: Llama 3.1 8B and 70B (layer 16 of 32 in the 8B shown); control effect measured as Cohen's d between score distributions under two imitation labels; up to N = 256 in-context examples; directions: logistic-regression axis versus early (PC 1-8) and late (PC 32-512) principal components.
limits: Authors do not claim full philosophical metacognition. Open models only. Late, low-variance directions are hard to control.
agent_relevance: Self-monitoring covers only a small, high-variance, interpretable part of the state. Most of what drives an answer is invisible to the model's own report.

source: Fleming, Lau (2014): sensitivity versus bias in confidence
finding: Gamma and phi correlations between confidence and accuracy are affected by bias. Type-2 d' of Kunimoto et al. (2001) assumes equal variance and is confounded by changes in metacognitive bias in simulation (Evans and Azzopardi 2007).
numbers: Evans and Azzopardi (2007) simulation; Masson and Rotello (2009) show bias in Goodman-Kruskal gamma.
limits: Methods review, no new participants.
agent_relevance: Many LLM calibration numbers use bias-sensitive metrics (e.g. ECE alone). Report AUROC2 or M-ratio next to ECE.

source: SEP Higher-Order Theories: rivals and objections (inner sense, computational cost, blindsight)
finding: Carruthers (2000) objects to inner-sense theory that monitors able to generate higher-order experiences would need heavy computation. Inner-sense also seems to allow believing one is in seeming-orange while in seeming-red. Blindsight and absent-minded driving are used as cases where first-order processing is intact without awareness of it.
numbers: Argument-level evidence; blindsight forced-choice accuracy can exceed 80% while subjects say they are guessing (Lau and Passingham 2006, a04).
limits: Philosophical objections, not experiments. Each side reads blindsight differently.
agent_relevance: A good answer does not prove the agent knows why it was good; report can be absent or wrong while task performance is fine.

source: Kadavath et al. (2022): P(IK) tracks context
finding: Predicted P(IK) rises when relevant source material is in context and when hints toward a math word problem solution are given. This shows the learned self-knowledge signal responds to what the model actually has available.
numbers: Reported qualitatively in the abstract; P(IK) trained on TriviaQA, Arithmetic, Lambada, Python function synthesis; value head on final token.
limits: Abstract-level claim, 2022 base models; honest-model training is flagged as future work.
agent_relevance: A cheap code-read probability can tell the scaffold when to fetch context or run a check, which fits G1 (doubt only on a signal).

source: Koriat (1997) Monitoring one's own knowledge during study: a cue-utilization approach to judgments of learning
finding: Feelings of knowing and judgments of learning are inferential: they are built from cues such as fluency, familiarity and ease of processing, which are often valid but can mislead. This is the experimental basis for treating metacognitive feelings as cue-based inference rather than direct access.
numbers: Not opened; no numbers claimed.
limits: Secondhand from memory of the literature.
agent_relevance: Supports using cues computed by code (agreement, margin, length) as monitor inputs and checking which cues are valid for which task.
